Beam tracks image the He-3 target

run_145 · stat090_0000 · arm A (det3) · nTOF partner 224670 · 2026-08-12 · PRELIMINARY

The waveform-first reconstruction, run for the first time on a fully nTOF-matched beam run, back-projects arm A's tracks to a compact source at the origin — the He-3 target is imaged. The reconstructed angle follows the point-source expectation tan θ = u / 235 mm across the plane, and the residual scale factor gives the first in-situ drift velocity at beam conditions: v ≈ 36.3 µm/ns, 15 % below the clean-gas Magboltz prior of 42.6.

What ran

run_145 (Aug 5, production statistics at the run_67 optimum: drift 700 V on all four chambers, resist A540/B540/C525/D520 V, Ar/iC4H10 90/10, 20 samples × 60 ns) is the only last-week run whose every sub-run carries complete nTOF matching — all three segments joined to nTOF run 224670 at ~95 % efficiency by the slim pipeline. Tracks come from the frozen MPGD26 wft/ chain (multi-track HEAD, single-track output bit-identical to the bench-validated code; the test suite passes on the analysis machine), driven by ntof_tracking/wft_beam.py with the bench→beam calibration transfer of PLAN_08: the impulse template and resistive-sharing kernel carry over as chamber hardware, the DAQ constants are replaced by run_145's, and v_drift starts as a Magboltz prior — which the imaging then measures. The per-event nTOF record is joined on eventId straight from the slim ntof_hits file; requiring a same-arm SiPM-wall hit is the purity cut.

The in-situ calibration

Positions never depend on v_drift; angles scale as 1/v. A ray from the origin crossing the strip plane at u must have tan θ = u/L exactly, so every inclined track measures the angle scale directly: ki = (ui/L)/tan θi.

quantityvaluecomment
v prior (Magboltz, clean 90/10, 233 V/cm)42.6 µm/nsbundle as seeded
v in-situ, imaging (arm A)36.3 µm/nsk = 1.17, |u| < 130 mm
bench wet-gas reference at this field23.3 µm/nsAr/iso 95/5 + H2O curve

36.3 sits between the clean-gas prediction and the wet bench curve — consistent with mildly wet gas after a month of flow, but deliberately quoted as an effective angle scale: the 20-sample readout window truncates the deepest columns and compresses large angles (the window-ablation prediction), and that compression is partially absorbed into k. For pointing and imaging purposes the effective scale is the right thing to use; separating true v from truncation needs the per-angle treatment.

What this does not show (yet)

  • The axial (Y) image is inconclusive. The y-plane pointing correlation is flat and the Y-profile of near-axis tracks shows no clear capsule concentration — y-plane angle quality and the in-plane offsets need work before the second imaging coordinate is real.
  • In-plane offsets are un-surveyed. The strip-map zero per arm is provisional (geometry caveat since PLAN_01); the ~5 mm off-axis ridge in Fig 2 is its likely signature. The natural next step is a two-parameter (u0, k) fit per arm — the imaging constrains both.
  • One arm, one sub-run. Arms C, B, D and sub-run 0001 are being reconstructed now; B's drift field is not set by its supply (degrador absent), so its v is nominal regardless.
  • Single-k calibration. First-order only; the |u| > 130 compression is excluded, not corrected.
Caveat under investigation. A discrepancy in the June cosmic-bench re-analysis (same frozen reconstruction code) was flagged the same day this note was written and is being tracked down in a parallel session. The beam results here share that code; if the cause lands in wft/ or the bundles rather than the campaign harness, the numbers on this page will be revisited. The target image itself is robust evidence the chain is not grossly broken at the position level.

Reproduce

ntof_tracking/wft_beam.py (bundle + reco per arm) and ntof_tracking/run145_target_imaging.py (pointing, image, k-scan) at repo HEAD; data under x17match/ on the desktop, slim products from out_224670. Frozen code commit in CODE_COMMIT.txt next to the deployed package.
